explain.say: Imagine a race where whoever is in front at the finish wins, even by one step. That is first past the post, a voting system used in the UK, India, Canada, the USA and Nigeria. Look at the board: five steps from your vote to a whole government.

faq.a: A constituency is an area of a country that elects its own representative. Each one has roughly the same number of voters.

faq.q: Do you need over half the votes to win?
faq.a: No. Under first past the post you only need more votes than any other candidate. With many candidates, someone can win with well under half.
asks: Do you need a majority to win?

faq.q: Why can seats and votes not match?
faq.a: Seats are won area by area. A party that narrowly wins many areas gets lots of seats, while a party that comes second everywhere can get very few, even with many votes overall.
asks: Why is first past the post unfair?

faq.q: Which countries use first past the post?
faq.a: The UK, India, Canada, the USA, Nigeria, Bangladesh and Malaysia use it for their main national elections.
asks: Who uses first past the post?

faq.q: What are the good and bad points of first past the post?
faq.a: Good: it is simple, results come quickly, and each area has one local member. Bad: many votes do not change the result, and smaller parties win fewer seats than their share of votes.
asks: Is first past the post a good system?

facts: In the 2024 UK general election, Labour won 411 of 650 seats with about 34% of the vote.
India's Lok Sabha has 543 constituencies, each electing one member by first past the post.

quiz.say: Ana gets 40 votes, Bo 35, Chidi 25. Who wins under first past the post?
quiz.show: Ana gets 40 votes, Bo 35, Chidi 25. Who wins under first past the post?
quiz.why: Ana has more votes than anyone else, and that is all first past the post needs.

wrong.2: First past the post has no rerun; the top candidate wins even without half.

quiz.say: Under first past the post, what do you need to win a seat?
quiz.show: Under first past the post, what do you need to win a seat?
quiz.why: A plurality, the most votes, is enough.

wrong.1: That is needed in two-round systems, not first past the post.
wrong.2: Money can help a campaign, but votes decide the seat.
